speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me identify the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you feel the room is spinning or is it more of a lightheaded feeling?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis (likely viral etiology). The patient's description of a constant, low-grade spinning sensation (vertigo) that improves with antihistamines, despite recent garlic consumption (which is not a known cause of acute vestibular neuritis), points strongly to an inner ear inflammation. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on the clinical presentation of acute unilateral vertigo in a young, otherwise healthy male.
